core_claim.quote: the hypothesis is that the prefrontal cortex plausibly plays a key role in consciousness because it supports essential cognitive mechanisms that underlie higher-order representations.

source.citation: Brown R, Lau H, LeDoux JE. Understanding the higher-order approach to consciousness. Trends in Cognitive Sciences 23(9):754-768, 2019. Quoted from the authors' preprint: Brown R, Lau H, LeDoux JE. The misunderstood higher-order approach to consciousness. PsyArXiv, 2019 (doi 10.31234/osf.io/xpy8h)

prediction.statement: Consciously perceiving something, compared with the same stimulus not perceived, involves prefrontal cortex (with parietal and insular cortex) acting on the sensory representation, also when the person does not have to report the stimulus.

first_stated.passage: our conclusion is that introspectively accessed states, which we view as phenomenally conscious experiences, are best described in terms of HORs that depend on the GNC, cortical circuits involving regions of the lateral and medial prefrontal cortex, posterior parietal cortex, and insular cortex (Fig. 2).

source.citation: LeDoux JE, Brown R. A higher-order theory of emotional consciousness. Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences 114(10):E2016-E2025, 2017

prediction.test_for: With stimuli matched and no report required, prefrontal cortex carries information about, or interacts with sensory cortex over, the stimuli that are consciously perceived, more than for the same stimuli not perceived.
prediction.test_against: With stimuli matched and no report required, awareness-related differences are confined to sensory cortex, and prefrontal cortex shows no awareness-related information or interaction by a method shown to be sensitive enough to find prefrontal effects in the same data.

study.name: Auditory awareness without report, measured with fMRI (inattentional deafness)

source.citation: Dellert T, Balster H, Schlossmacher I, Bruchmann M, Moeck R, Straube T. Neural correlates of consciousness in an auditory no-report fMRI study. bioRxiv 2025.05.16.654468; published in Current Biology, 2025 (10.1016/j.cub.2025.10.026)

data_collected.basis: The preprint gives no collection dates (methods searched 2026-11-20); the data were collected before the preprint appeared.

passages.text: Comparing brain responses to the critical sounds between aware and unaware participants while controlling for correlates of sensory and postperceptual processing revealed that auditory awareness was associated with significantly increased activity in secondary auditory but not in fronto-parietal areas.

source.citation: Dellert T, Balster H, Schlossmacher I, Bruchmann M, Moeck R, Straube T. Neural correlates of consciousness in an auditory no-report fMRI study. bioRxiv 2025.05.16.654468; published in Current Biology, 2025 (10.1016/j.cub.2025.10.026)

passages.text: Together, these results do not support a key role of the lateral PFC in conscious perception (Brown et al., 2019; Mashour et al., 2020; Panagiotaropoulos, 2024).

source.citation: Dellert T, Balster H, Schlossmacher I, Bruchmann M, Moeck R, Straube T. Neural correlates of consciousness in an auditory no-report fMRI study. bioRxiv 2025.05.16.654468; published in Current Biology, 2025 (10.1016/j.cub.2025.10.026)

passages.text: While the left middle and superior frontal gyrus and inferior frontal junction showed significant stimulus effects in the aware but not the unaware group, the awareness contrast did not reveal significant effects in these areas. This was because sub-threshold frontal activity occurred even in the absence of awareness, cancelling according effects out in the NCC contrast.

source.citation: Dellert T, Balster H, Schlossmacher I, Bruchmann M, Moeck R, Straube T. Neural correlates of consciousness in an auditory no-report fMRI study. bioRxiv 2025.05.16.654468; published in Current Biology, 2025 (10.1016/j.cub.2025.10.026)
